title: Account reconciliation software: what it does and how to test it
description: How software matches your books to bank and other records, what it can and cannot settle on its own, and how to test it on your own accounts.
summary: Account reconciliation compares your accounting records with the bank's records and explains every difference. Software does the matching, including one payment that covers many invoices, and leaves a short list for a person to research.

example.input: A month of bank transactions and your ledger entries for the same account.
example.output: Matched pairs, a short list of unmatched items with likely reasons, and suggested entries for bank fees and interest.

howToTest: Take one closed month that your team already reconciled by hand and keep the final signed result.
Load the same raw bank data and ledger into the software and let it run.
Compare its matches with your signed result. Count wrong matches separately from missed matches.
Check that every item it could not match shows a clear reason a person can act on.
Repeat on a messy month with many split or combined payments.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy when you reconcile many accounts monthly and your accounting system or an add-on already imports bank data.
buyVsBuild.build: Build only when your matching rules are unusual, such as many-to-many matches across your own internal systems.

watchOuts: A wrong automatic match hides a problem. Reconciliation exists to find errors and fraud, so review the matches too.
After any system update, check again that the matching still works as expected.
Automation does not replace the policy: who reconciles, how often, and who reviews the result.
Separate duties. The person who records transactions should not be the only person who reconciles them.

resources.name: Washington State Auditor: Best Practices for Bank Reconciliations
resources.what: A government guide to reconciliation policy, frequency, automation and fraud controls such as Positive Pay.

sources.name: Washington State Auditor: Best Practices for Bank Reconciliations (March 2026)
sources.what: Says reconciliation can identify fraud, flag bank errors and highlight your own mistakes, and says some systems can automatically reconcile most or all items, including one-to-many matches, if you periodically verify they work.
